title: Eye
shortDescription: Every labelled part of the eye and the basic pathway light travels to become vision.
genZNote: Helps you see the world — one clear pathway from light to signal.

illustration.alt: Labelled cross-section illustration of the eye
illustration.caption: Eye — Cellfie Human Anatomy

structures.name: Cornea
structures.description: Clear, curved front surface of the eye.
structures.function: Does most of the eye's light bending (refraction).

structures.name: Iris
structures.description: Colored ring of muscle around the pupil.
structures.function: Controls pupil size, regulating how much light enters.

structures.name: Pupil
structures.description: The dark opening at the center of the iris.
structures.function: The actual opening light passes through.

structures.name: Retina
structures.description: Light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye.
structures.function: Converts light into neural signals via photoreceptors (rods and cones).

structures.name: Fovea
structures.description: Small pit in the retina's center.
structures.function: Area of sharpest vision, packed densely with cones.

structures.name: Optic nerve
structures.description: Nerve leaving the back of the eye.
structures.function: Carries visual signals from the retina to the brain.

structures.name: Sclera
structures.description: Tough white outer coat of the eyeball.
structures.function: Protects and maintains the eye's shape.

structures.name: Ciliary body
structures.description: Ring of tissue behind the iris.
structures.function: Controls the lens's shape and produces aqueous humor.

pathways.title: Basic Vision Pathway
steps: Passes through the pupil (size set by the iris)
Signal travels via the optic nerve
Processed by the occipital lobe of the brain

comparisons.distinction: The cornea does most of the eye's fixed light-bending; the lens fine-tunes focus by changing shape.
The retina is the whole light-sensitive layer; the fovea is a small, especially sharp-vision pit within it.

questions.prompt: In the labelled eye illustration, which structure controls how much light enters by adjusting pupil size?
questions.explanation: The iris is the colored muscular ring that controls pupil size, regulating light entry.
optionNotes: Bends light but does not control pupil size.
Converts light to signals, doesn't control light entry.

questions.prompt: Which nerve carries visual signals from the eye to the brain?
questions.explanation: The optic nerve carries signals from the retina's photoreceptors to the brain's visual processing areas.
optionNotes: Carries facial sensory/motor signals, not vision specifically.

sections.heading: Structures of the Eye
bullets: Cornea — clear front surface; does most of the eye's light bending (refraction).
Iris — the colored ring of muscle that controls pupil size.
Pupil — the opening in the iris that light passes through.
Lens — fine-tunes focus by changing shape.
Sclera — the tough white outer coat of the eyeball.
Ciliary body — muscle that changes the lens's shape for focusing.
Retina — the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye that converts light into nerve signals.
Fovea — a small pit in the retina with the sharpest vision, densely packed with cone cells.
Optic nerve — carries visual signals from the retina to the brain.

sections.heading: Basic Pathway of Vision
sections.body: Light enters through the cornea → passes through the pupil (its size set by the iris) → is fine-focused by the lens → forms an image on the retina → the retina converts light into electrical signals → the optic nerve carries these signals to the brain for interpretation.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The eye focuses light onto the retina, which converts it into signals the optic nerve carries to the brain.
keyFacts: The cornea provides most of the eye's focusing power; the lens fine-tunes it.
The iris controls pupil size, regulating how much light enters.
The retina, not the lens, actually converts light into nerve signals.
The fovea is the retina's region of sharpest vision.
commonConfusion: Cornea (fixed, does most of the focusing) is often confused with lens (adjustable, fine-tunes focus).

highYieldFacts: Light-to-signal conversion happens at the retina, not at the lens or cornea.
The fovea is the point of sharpest central vision.
commonTraps: Don't say the lens does most of the eye's refraction — the cornea contributes more focusing power overall.
mustRemember: Pathway: cornea → pupil (via iris) → lens → retina → optic nerve → brain.
